refinance.title: Finance $3,000 refinance costs without treating them as free
refinance.inputs: $250,000 current balance; $1,800 P&I; current 6%; replacement 5% for twenty years; $3,000 fees financed; no cash out or points.
steps: Add costs to get a $253,000 new principal.
Calculate the replacement P&I payment and retain the higher remaining balance caused by financing costs.
At month sixty, subtract new interest and the closing cost once from current interest; simple payment recovery is a separate screen.

refinance.title: Keep an increased refinance payment distinct from simple recovery
refinance.inputs: $250,000 current balance; $1,800 P&I; current 6%; replacement 5% for fifteen years; $3,000 upfront costs; no points or cash out.
steps: Amortize the replacement over 180 monthly periods.
Subtract its payment from the current $1,800; the result is negative.
Do not report a positive or zero simple payment-recovery time when the monthly payment rises.
refinance.answer: Monthly payment reduction: -$176.98; simple payment recovery not applicable.

mortgage-payoff.title: Time an annual mortgage extra payment at month twelve
mortgage-payoff.inputs: $120,000 current balance; 6%; $2,500 regular monthly P&I; $3,000 extra at month twelve and every twelve payments afterward.
steps: Retain the contractual payment and apply the extra only at each annual scheduled month.
Accrue interest on opening principal, apply payment and cap the final installment.
Compare with $250 extra monthly as a different timing pattern; extra cash stops when the loan is repaid.

mortgage-payoff.title: Delay a $10,000 mortgage principal payment until month twenty-four
mortgage-payoff.inputs: $120,000 current balance; 6%; $2,500 regular monthly P&I; one $10,000 extra at scheduled month twenty-four; no other extras.
steps: Keep the first twenty-three scheduled payments unchanged.
Apply the lump sum after month twenty-four interest.
Compare its remaining interest with the same lump sum in month one, excluding opportunity returns and prepayment penalties.

rent-vs-buy.title: Hold home appreciation at zero in the rent-versus-buy model
rent-vs-buy.inputs: $400,000 home; 20% down; 6% thirty-year loan; $2,400 starting monthly rent; original guide ownership and transaction costs; no income-tax benefit. 0% home appreciation, 5% portfolio return.
steps: Keep the purchased home’s gross value constant and still subtract the selling cost and remaining loan at each annual checkpoint.
Read buyer and renter wealth in the same year-ten schedule row.
Keep the full thirty-year output separate from that checkpoint and do not call the first annual crossing a permanent lead.

rent-vs-buy.title: Remove investment growth without hiding rent-versus-buy funding gaps
rent-vs-buy.inputs: $400,000 home; 20% down; 6% thirty-year loan; $2,400 starting monthly rent; original guide ownership and transaction costs; no income-tax benefit. 3% appreciation, 0% portfolio return.
steps: Set opportunity return to zero while continuing all monthly cash-flow deposits or withdrawals; inspect negative account figures as unfunded shortfalls.
Read buyer and renter wealth in the same year-ten schedule row.
Keep the full thirty-year output separate from that checkpoint and do not call the first annual crossing a permanent lead.
